evals.prompt: Write the brief for a Codex review-and-fix pass over a lane's three commits that change capture readback in the render-graph runtime.
evals.expected_output: Writes a self-contained brief to a lane-named file: a one-sentence frame naming the domains, the review worktree path (the author's clean worktree or a detached tree at its head under .claude/worktrees/<name>, with no branch created for the pass) and branch or detached head plus the author's receiving branch, with edit-only and don't-commit; an exact commit range with each commit listed and its message to be read; the contract in the code's own names with decisions already taken; a hunt list per area drawing on rendering's runtime-contracts reference (pinned or copied pixels, leases, completion, epochs); the evidence already gathered; and the verbatim rules and instructions blocks including compiling what it changed and the end-list format. Pauses other edits and commits on the author's branch until landing.

evals.prompt: The Codex review pass over a Claude-written lane finished with four fixes and one open finding, uncommitted. How do you land it?
evals.expected_output: Checks each finding against current files and records the round and fix range; commits the pass unbuilt as a local WIP; has a Claude agent with fixes enabled build the touched projects and the solution, prove each new law red with its fix withheld and green with it, run the reached suites and check forms, settle the open finding, and review round 1's fix diff alone for blockers as round 2. For doc-only fixes, uses documentation checks without laws or builds except for XML changes. Sends remaining round 2 blockers to the lead for a ruling before further repairs; verifies those repairs without a third review round. Replaces only unpublished pass commits with area: sentence commits carrying the evidence and no Co-Authored-By trailer; lands a detached pass with git merge --ff-only from the clean author's worktree, stopping on divergence without resetting or rebasing. Keeps WIPs and verification repairs unpublished, merges the current integration tip, runs final required checks, takes granted GPU legs or reports them owed, and pushes the working branch fast-forward only after its gates pass.

evals.prompt: A Codex-written lane needs its review. Who reviews it, and when does the loop end?
evals.expected_output: A Claude agent (Sonnet or Opus) runs round 1 over the lane with fixes enabled. A Claude verifier checks its fixes so verification repairs stay Claude-written. If round 1 makes blocker fixes, including documentation fixes, the companion's Codex task --write pass runs round 2 over round 1's fix diff alone. The loop ends when a pass reports no blockers, and after round 2 at the latest; non-blocking findings and their fixes never trigger another review. An unchanged pass skips WIP creation and fix verification; unresolved blockers go to the lead. The lead rules on what round 2 still raises (a scoped fix, an open item, or a dismissal with its reason); subsequent verification runs no fresh hunt or third review round.

evals.prompt: Scoping a review: `git log --oneline A..B` lists three commits, so you write the scope as `git diff A..B` and call them the lane's commits. Is the scope right?
evals.expected_output: Checks `git merge-base --is-ancestor A B` rather than inferring ancestry from the log. Explains that the two-dot log selects commits reachable from B but not A, while the two-dot diff compares endpoint trees, so a divergent A can contribute reversed changes to the review diff. When A is an ancestor, pins A as a commit for the exact range; otherwise pins the merge base and reviews its diff to B (`git diff A...B` has that meaning). Lists each lane commit by commit and subject and names any already-reviewed merge work as an exclusion; exclusions do not turn a divergent tip-to-tip diff into the lane's change.

evals.prompt: A Codex review-and-fix pass returns fixes and two new laws, and reports that its build exited 1 with access denied to an SDK directory, so it ran no tests, and that format passed with a CLI copy it found in the tree. What do you accept?
evals.expected_output: Accepts nothing it claims to have run: a sandbox that could not reach the SDK proved nothing, and a format result from a stale CLI copy does not judge the head's rules. Commits the pass as a local WIP, then builds outside the sandbox, proves each new law red with its fix withheld and green with it (through `puck laws prove`), runs the touched test classes, and reruns the format and link checks from a fresh copy of the head's own CLI, before replacing the WIP.

evals.prompt: A Codex implementation pass ended with a question and no edits: may it temporarily remove a project reference so the prescribed build does not also build another project? How do you proceed?
evals.expected_output: Treats the pass as not done. Answers from the brief and the repository rules (here: keep the prescribed command and the project file unchanged, since a transitive build through an existing reference is expected), writes the answer to a prompt file, and continues the same thread with the companion's `task --resume-last`, telling it to finish without further questions. Tightens future briefs so the pass answers its own questions from the code and the brief.

evals.prompt: A qualification run is building from a clean worktree while executing canary, counters and parity legs serially. A review-and-fix pass is ready to launch with --write, and its edits seem unrelated to those workloads. Where and when do you launch it?
evals.expected_output: Does not launch a writing pass into the tree supplying the active run, even for apparently unrelated edits. Waits until that run finishes or uses a separate review worktree at the intended head. Recognizes that a mid-run edit changes the source state the run reuses, so the clean starting tree does not make concurrent writes safe.
